title: Ask the author: a question's round trip
summary: Panopticon runs AI agents that write PRs. This PR lets a reviewer send a question to the agent that wrote the code, and get the answer back inside the review. The tour follows one question the whole way: find the author, file it, wrap it, deliver it, collect the reply, hand it back.
author: agent:claude (review tour)

steps.title: 1 · Who wrote this code?
steps.note: Background: panopticon is a system that runs AI agents, each working on its own task and opening a PR when done. This PR adds a way to ask the agent that wrote some code a question while you review it. Step one is finding that agent: the review tool sends the PR's web address here, and this function looks up which task (and so which agent) produced it.

steps.title: 2 · Filing the question
steps.note: The reviewer's question gets saved as an 'ask' attached to the task. Only one question can be waiting per task at a time. If you try to file a second one too early you get a 'still working on the last one' error, and if the agent is long gone you get a 'nobody home' error so the review tool can offer a stand-in instead.

steps.title: 3 · The four stages of a question
steps.note: A question moves through simple stages, like a package you can track. PENDING means filed but not yet handed to the agent. DELIVERED means the agent has it, and ANSWERED means the reply came back. GONE means the agent's saved session no longer exists, so this question can never be answered by the original author.

steps.title: 4 · Writing the letter
steps.note: The question is wrapped in a letter before delivery. The letter starts with a tracking code, which is how the reply gets matched back to the question later. It also includes ground rules: if the agent's task is already finished, the letter says 'just answer, do not change any code'. For work still in progress the rules are softer, since a good question sometimes deserves a fix.

steps.title: 5 · The mail carrier
steps.note: A background loop on each machine checks every task for a waiting question. If the agent is running right now, the letter is typed straight into its terminal. If the agent's saved memory was deleted, the question is marked GONE. If the agent is asleep but its memory survives, we wake it up, which is the next step.

steps.title: 6 · Waking up a retired author
steps.note: Agents whose work is merged are normally left alone, but asking them a question is a special case. Their conversation memory is kept on disk, so we can restart the agent from exactly where it left off, with the letter as the first thing it sees. If two machines try to wake the same agent, only one wins and the other backs off.

steps.title: 7 · Collecting the reply
steps.note: When the agent finishes talking, a small hook reads its conversation log. It looks for the letter with our tracking code and copies out everything the agent said in response, stopping at the next incoming message. If there is no reply yet it quietly returns nothing and tries again next time.

steps.title: 8 · The answer comes home
steps.note: The reply is saved and the question is stamped ANSWERED. The review tool has been checking in on the question every few seconds, so the answer now pops up in the reviewer's answers panel. It is labeled as the author's claim rather than verified truth, because the agent is explaining its own work.
